headline: Nations League: Germany crush Netherlands 5-0 to seal Group A2 top spot
teaser: Florian Wirtz scores twice while Derry Scherhant, Nico Schlotterbeck, and Brajan Gruda add goals as Germany inflict the Netherlands' heaviest defeat in 67 years to win Group A2.
story:
Germany produced a masterclass of attacking football on Monday night, 16 November, dismantling traditional rivals the Netherlands 5-0 in Leipzig to capture first place in UEFA Nations League Group A2.

Julian Nagelsmann's side took control late in the first half when 23-year-old winger Derry Scherhant opened the scoring on 41 minutes with a crisp angled drive. The floodgates opened after the break as Florian Wirtz curled home a magnificent 20-yard effort on the hour mark. Nico Schlotterbeck headed in a corner on 65 minutes, substitute Brajan Gruda slotted home a fourth on 72 minutes, and Wirtz completed his brace in the 77th minute with a delicate chip over Bart Verbruggen.

The 5-0 scoreline represents the Netherlands' worst defeat in an international fixture since 1959. Although both nations advance to the quarter-finals in March 2027, Germany secure seeded status while Ronald Koeman's squad face an inquest after an uncharacteristically fragile defensive collapse.
whyCareReason: Germany hand their fiercest rivals their worst defeat since 1959, securing the top seed in Nations League Group A2 in emphatic fashion.
stakes: Germany finish top of Group A2 to earn seeded quarter-final status in March 2027, sending the Dutch through as unseeded runners-up.
rivalryAngle: Historic renewal of one of international football's fiercest rivalries, ending in unprecedented German dominance before 42,000 in Leipzig.
funFacts: The 5-0 defeat was the Netherlands' heaviest margin of defeat in any international match since November 1959.
Florian Wirtz recorded his second career international brace, scoring in the 60th and 77th minutes.
Germany scored four goals in a blistering 17-minute second-half stretch.
